hints: Identify the parameters of the normal distribution: mean $\mu = 20$ and standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{49} = 7$.
Use the complement rule to find the cumulative probability: $\mathrm{P}(X < k) = 1 - 0.25 = 0.75$.
Look up the $z$-score corresponding to $\Phi(z) = 0.75$ in the standard normal distribution table.
Set up the standardisation equation $z = \dfrac{k - 20}{7}$ and solve for $k$.
walkthrough:
Convert the upper tail probability into a cumulative probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > k) = 0.25 \implies \mathrm{P}(X < k) = 1 - 0.25 = 0.75$$

Find the critical $z$-value from the normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(z) = 0.75 \implies z = 0.674$$

Set up the standardisation equation and solve for $k$:
$$\dfrac{k - 20}{7} = 0.674$$
$$k - 20 = 7 \times 0.674 = 4.718$$
$$k = 20 + 4.718 = 24.718 \approx 24.7$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Start by identifying the given distribution of $X$:
$$X \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, \sigma^2) = \mathrm{N}(20, 49)$$
Here, the mean is $\mu = 20$, the variance is $\sigma^2 = 49$, and the standard deviation is:
$$\sigma = \sqrt{49} = 7$$

We are given that $\mathrm{P}(X > k) = 0.25$. Because standard normal tables list cumulative probabilities $\mathrm{P}(Z < z) = \Phi(z)$, apply the complement rule:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < k) = 1 - 0.25 = 0.75$$

Look up the probability $0.75$ in the standard normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(0.67) = 0.7486, \quad \text{difference for } 4 \text{ is } 13 \implies \Phi(0.674) = 0.7499 \approx 0.7500$$
So the standard normal score is:
$$z = 0.674$$

Write down the standardisation formula relating $X$ to $Z$:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$$
Substitute $Z = 0.674$, $X = k$, $\mu = 20$, and $\sigma = 7$:
$$0.674 = \frac{k - 20}{7}$$

Multiply both sides by 7 to clear the denominator:
$$k - 20 = 7 \times 0.674 = 4.718$$
Add 20 to both sides:
$$k = 20 + 4.718 = 24.718$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $k = 24.7$.
